title: Determination of Effective Synaptic Conductances Using Somatic Voltage Clamp
author: Songting Li
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wm4fc8w

steps.title: Clamp soma and record currents
steps.instruction: Set the somatic voltage clamp to a series of holding potentials, use dynamic clamp to inject matched excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) synaptic conductances onto the dendrite, and record the resulting synaptic currents at the soma while keeping the dendritic inputs constant across voltages.

substeps.instruction: Select a range of somatic holding voltages.
Program the dynamic clamp to deliver identical E and I synaptic inputs on the dendrite for each holding voltage.
Measure and log the synaptic current arriving at the soma for each voltage.

steps.title: Fit I‑V relation and correct potentials
steps.instruction: For each time point, fit a linear relationship between the somatic holding voltage and the recorded synaptic current, extract the intercept of the I‑V curve, and correct the holding potentials using the calculated liquid‑junction potential.

substeps.instruction: Perform linear regression of current versus voltage.
Read the intercept value from the fitted line.
Adjust the recorded holding potentials by subtracting the liquid‑junction potential as described by Barry et al. (1994).

steps.title: Vary reversal potential and repeat
steps.instruction: Change the reversal potential of the dynamic‑clamp‑generated synaptic inputs to a new value, then repeat the voltage‑clamp recordings and I‑V fitting to obtain a second set of intercepts.

substeps.instruction: Set a new reversal potential for the dynamic‑clamp conductances.
Repeat step 1 (clamp soma and record currents) with the new reversal potential.
Repeat step 2 (fit I‑V relation and correct potentials) for the new data.

steps.title: Calculate effective conductances
steps.instruction: Use the intercepts from the two I‑V relations (original and altered reversal potentials) to solve for the effective excitatory and inhibitory synaptic conductances at each time point.
